title.en: Take notes from a health segment
title.es: Tomar notas de un segmento de salud

es: Tomar notas de un segmento de audio sobre salud separando la idea principal, los detalles, los ejemplos y la recomendación.

teaching.en: Before you jot down anything, listen for the gist: the main idea usually appears in the first sentences or in the final summary.
teaching.es: Antes de apuntar nada, escucha la idea general: la idea principal suele aparecer en las primeras frases o en el resumen final.
teaching.explanationEs: El gist es la esencia del mensaje; jot down = apuntar rápido, con pocas palabras.
segments: Before you jot down anything, listen for the gist: the main idea
usually appears in the first sentences or in the final summary.
teaching.audioText: Before you jot down anything, listen for the gist: the main idea usually appears in the first sentences or in the final summary.

teaching.en: A detail supports the main idea with research, figures or an example, for instance a study of a short nap after lunch, and it often follows markers such as first or also.
teaching.es: Un detalle apoya la idea principal con investigación, cifras o un ejemplo, por ejemplo un estudio sobre una siesta corta tras comer, y suele ir tras marcadores como first o also.
teaching.explanationEs: El detalle no es el mensaje central: lo demuestra, lo mide o lo ilustra.
segments: A detail supports the main idea with research, figures or an example, for instance a study
of a short nap after lunch, and it often follows markers such as first or also.
teaching.audioText: A detail supports the main idea with research, figures or an example, for instance a study of a short nap after lunch, and it often follows markers such as first or also.

teaching.en: Jot down keywords rather than whole sentences: a good note is short enough to read at a glance but complete enough to rebuild the idea later.
teaching.es: Apunta palabras clave en lugar de frases enteras: una buena nota es lo bastante corta para leerla de un vistazo y lo bastante completa para reconstruir la idea después.
teaching.explanationEs: Note = nota; escribe palabras clave, cifras y nombres, no la frase completa.
segments: Jot down keywords rather than whole sentences: a good note is short enough
to read at a glance but complete enough to rebuild the idea later.
teaching.audioText: Jot down keywords rather than whole sentences: a good note is short enough to read at a glance but complete enough to rebuild the idea later.

teaching.en: The speaker adds a caveat whenever the evidence has limits, for example when a study followed only a small group of volunteers.
teaching.es: El locutor añade una salvedad siempre que las pruebas tienen límites, por ejemplo cuando un estudio siguió solo a un grupo pequeño de voluntarios.
teaching.explanationEs: Una caveat limita hasta dónde vale la evidencia; suele ir tras but, however o even so.
segments: The speaker adds a caveat whenever the evidence has limits, for
example when a study followed only a small group of volunteers.
teaching.audioText: The speaker adds a caveat whenever the evidence has limits, for example when a study followed only a small group of volunteers.

teaching.en: The benefit of caffeine is sharper concentration during the day, whereas the risk is a chronic lack of sleep if you drink it too late.
teaching.es: El beneficio de la cafeína es una concentración más aguda durante el día, mientras que el riesgo es una falta crónica de sueño si se toma demasiado tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Benefit y risk son detalles de signo opuesto: lo que se gana y lo que se arriesga.
segments: The benefit of caffeine is sharper concentration during the day, whereas the risk
is a chronic lack of sleep if you drink it too late.
teaching.audioText: The benefit of caffeine is sharper concentration during the day, whereas the risk is a chronic lack of sleep if you drink it too late.

teaching.en: The speaker's recommendation closes the segment: put the phone away an hour before bed, so that your body can wind down.
teaching.es: La recomendación del locutor cierra el segmento: guarda el móvil una hora antes de dormir, para que tu cuerpo se relaje.
teaching.explanationEs: La recomendación es lo que el locutor te pide hacer; casi siempre va al final. Wind down = relajarse.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la idea principal que anotarías del inicio del segmento.

choices.text: Teenagers sleep less because they start school earlier than adults do.
Late phone use cuts teenagers' sleep and can harm their mood and memory.
Most teenagers switch off their phones at ten and sleep very well.

feedback.es: La presentadora enlaza el uso del móvil con menos sueño y con efectos en el ánimo y la memoria: es el mensaje central.

hint.es: Busca la frase que resume tanto la causa como la consecuencia.

origin.audio: Teenagers who use their phones until midnight usually sleep an hour less than those who switch off at ten. That is why the presenter begins with a warning: poor sleep is not a small problem, because it affects mood and memory.

prompt.es: Completa: «Apunta rápido la cifra clave y la recomendación.»

feedback.es: Jot down es apuntar rápido, con pocas palabras: justo lo que hace falta al tomar notas de un audio.

hint.es: Es un verbo de tres letras que significa apuntar algo deprisa.

origin.text: Do not copy whole sentences while you listen. ___ down the key figure and the recommendation, and leave the rest for later.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El locutor añade una salvedad sobre el tamaño del estudio.»

answer.text: The speaker adds a caveat about the size of the study

feedback.es: Una caveat limita el alcance de la evidencia; aquí, el tamaño del estudio.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto y termina con el complemento del estudio.

prompt.es: Escucha el informe y elige qué salvedad menciona la investigadora.

choices.text: The people who walked were all young, so older people may not benefit.
Only people who walked for an hour a day felt any benefit.
The study covered only a year, so lasting effects are unclear.

feedback.es: Tras however, la investigadora limita el alcance del estudio: solo duró un año, así que los efectos a largo plazo no están claros.

origin.audio: A large survey found that adults who walk for thirty minutes a day are less likely to feel anxious. The benefit appears after only a few weeks. However, the researcher adds a caveat: the survey followed people for just one year, so effects over many years are still unclear. Her recommendation is small: start with ten minutes after lunch, and increase slowly.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada nota con el nivel del esquema al que pertenece.

pairs: Daily walks make adults less anxious.
Survey of four thousand adults over a year.
Results may not last, the researcher warns.
Start with ten minutes after lunch.

feedback.es: Cada nota cumple un papel: el mensaje central, el dato que lo apoya, el límite de la evidencia o el consejo final.

pairs: Daily walks make adults less anxious.
Survey of four thousand adults over a year.
Results may not last, the researcher warns.
Start with ten minutes after lunch.

prompt.es: Un compañero ha etiquetado estas notas. ¿Qué corrección harías?

choices.text: The last line is advice, so it should be labelled as the recommendation.
The survey line is a limit on the evidence, so it should not be a detail.
The first line is only an example, so it should be the recommendation.

feedback.es: «Start with ten minutes…» le pide algo al oyente: es la recomendación, no un dato que apoye la idea.

origin.text: Notes: Main idea — daily walking improves mood. Detail — a survey of four thousand adults over one year. Detail — start with ten minutes after lunch and increase slowly.

prompt.es: Escucha el segmento y elige la idea principal que anotarías.

choices.text: Coffee keeps people awake for a while but has no other effect.
Late caffeine can damage sleep even when people do not notice it.
Young volunteers sleep badly whenever they drink any coffee.

feedback.es: El experimento contradice la creencia habitual: los voluntarios durmieron menos sin notar diferencia, que es el mensaje central.

origin.audio: In today's health segment, the presenter looks at caffeine. Many people believe that a late coffee only keeps them awake for a while, but a new experiment suggests otherwise. Volunteers who drank a strong coffee six hours before bed slept about forty minutes less, even though most of them said they felt no different. The researchers add a caveat: the group was small, and everybody was young. Even so, the presenter's advice is clear. Write down the time of your last coffee for a week, and if you sleep badly, move it earlier in the day.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué da a entender el consejo final.

choices.text: That everybody should stop drinking coffee completely.
That the experiment proved the effect for all adults.
That each person can test the effect on their own sleep.

feedback.es: Pide registrar la hora del último café durante una semana y ajustarla solo si se duerme mal: propone comprobarlo uno mismo.

origin.audio: In today's health segment, the presenter looks at caffeine. Many people believe that a late coffee only keeps them awake for a while, but a new experiment suggests otherwise. Volunteers who drank a strong coffee six hours before bed slept about forty minutes less, even though most of them said they felt no different. The researchers add a caveat: the group was small, and everybody was young. Even so, the presenter's advice is clear. Write down the time of your last coffee for a week, and if you sleep badly, move it earlier in the day.

prompt.es: Completa: «Escucha primero la idea general y apunta después los detalles.»

feedback.es: El gist es la esencia del mensaje: se capta antes de apuntar los detalles que la apoyan.

origin.text: When a segment is long, do not write anything at the start. Listen first for the ___ of the message, and only then add the details.

prompt.es: Escribe tus notas en inglés: idea principal, un detalle, una salvedad y la recomendación.

answer.text: Main idea: a short nap helps tired adults concentrate. Detail: two hundred office workers were followed for a month. Caveat: the workers chose when to nap. Recommendation: nap before three o'clock and set an alarm.
accepted: Main idea: a short nap helps tired adults concentrate. Detail: two hundred office workers were followed for a month. Caveat: the workers chose when to nap. Recommendation: nap before three o'clock and set an alarm.

Main idea: a twenty-minute nap helps tired adults concentrate. Detail: researchers followed two hundred workers for a month. Caveat: the workers chose when they napped. Recommendation: nap before three and set an alarm.

Main idea: short naps help tired people concentrate. Detail: the study followed 200 office workers for a month. Caveat: the workers chose when to nap, so the results may be affected. Advice: nap before 3 pm and set an alarm.

feedback.es: Las notas separan el mensaje central, el dato que lo apoya, el límite de la evidencia y el consejo, con palabras clave y sin copiar frases enteras.

origin.text: A new report on afternoon naps finds that a twenty-minute nap helps tired adults concentrate, while naps longer than an hour leave many people feeling heavy. Researchers followed two hundred office workers for a month. The authors admit that the workers chose when to nap, which may have changed the results. Their advice: nap before three o'clock and set an alarm.

evidenceGroups: chose the time of their naps
chose when they took a nap

prompt.es: Lee el correo de la tutora. ¿Qué pretende conseguir con él?

choices.text: To persuade the student to write less and choose what matters.
To praise the student for writing such complete notes.
To warn the student that the recording is no longer available.

feedback.es: Critica el exceso de notas y fija qué conservar (gist, cifras, consejo): quiere que el alumno seleccione, no que transcriba.

origin.text: Tutor's email: Your notes copy almost every sentence of the recording. That does not help you revise. Next time, keep only the gist, two or three figures and the speaker's advice, and leave everything else out.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Anota la cifra, no toda la frase que la rodea.»

answer.text: Write down the figure, not the whole sentence around it

feedback.es: La nota conserva el dato clave y deja fuera la frase completa: write down + dato, not + resto.

prompt.es: Completa: «Guarda el móvil una hora antes de dormir para que tu cuerpo se relaje.»

feedback.es: Wind down es relajarse poco a poco; la recomendación cierra el segmento con un consejo práctico.

origin.text: The presenter finished with her advice: «Put the phone away an hour before bed, so that your body can wind ___.»
